revisions.body: The handoff is best heard as framing: it places the account before its listeners without repeating the preceding movement into the scene.
A useful listening cue: hear the inherited order as a demand placed on human beings.

body: "The opening gives the handoff a physical rhythm. Timaeus describes release from the difficult passage of his logos as rest after a long journey, then formally transfers the next logos to Critias according to their arrangements. One way to hear the metaphor is that Critias inherits a burden already in motion: the transition is not a new beginning, but a change of speaker carrying the discourse forward. That sense of inherited burden is an interpretation; the passage itself establishes the journey image and the formal transfer."

body: "The passage does not present the past as wholly erased. It preserves the rulers’ names, while their deeds have vanished and the surviving remnant knows only a few brief reports alongside those names. Read this as a portrait of selective transmission: a name can carry continuity without carrying a full account of conduct. The result is an inherited past with a clear limit—names remain, but the deeds they once identified cannot be recovered in full."
